properties.statement:
ROOT-CAUSE PASS ON ALEX'S UPGRADE REPORT, 2026-08-29. The cause is not the installer. ⚠️ AND THIS NODE'S OWN FIRST DRAFT OVERSTATED THE FIX — corrected below, measured rather than argued.

═══ ① THE CAUSE, READ OUT OF THE CODE ═══

`ensure_server_async` (`shared.rs`) asks an existing rendezvous exactly two questions: **is it for THIS graph**, and **does something ANSWER at that URL** (`else if probe(&r.url).await { attach }`). It then attaches. **`r.version` is never read.**

🛑 THE FIELD EXISTS WITH ITS PURPOSE WRITTEN ON IT. `Rendezvous.version`: *"so a FUTURE VERSION CAN REFUSE AN INCOMPATIBLE PEER rather than guess."* Published, intended, and the refusal deferred to a future that has not come.

⭐ AND SOMEBODY CHOSE THIS DELIBERATELY, in `relaunchable_exe_from`'s doc: *"The resulting version skew is exactly what `served_by.stale` already reports, so it is visible rather than silent."* Defensible for the stranded-session problem it solved; it is also the reasoning that produced Alex's bug, because it treats *reported in a JSON field* as *the operator will know*.

═══ 🛑 ② THE INSTALLER IS A TRIGGER — AND SO IS A VERSION CHECK ═══

Applying the step-⑥ test to BOTH candidate fixes, measured:

    instance                                   install.sh fix   version check
    Alex, macOS, installer upgrade 0.39→0.42        YES              YES
    this dev session, Linux, x6 (cargo build)        NO               NO
    Anthony, 2026-08-08 (rebuild)                    NO               NO

🛑 **THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS NODE CLAIMED A VERSION CHECK "WOULD HAVE CAUGHT EVERY ONE OF THEM". FALSE.** Measured: `Cargo.toml` read `0.42.0` all day, and every one of the five daemons this session stopped published `version: 0.42.0` against a client that was also `0.42.0`. **A version-string check catches ZERO of the six rebuild instances** — its coverage is the same as fixing the installer, the release-upgrade path only.

⇒ **THE COMPARAND MUST DISTINGUISH TWO BUILDS OF ONE VERSION.** A version string cannot. `(dev, inode)` of the executable can, in one `stat()`: `cargo build` and `install -m 755` both write a NEW file, so the running daemon holds the old inode while a fresh client resolves the new one. Same file → same inode → correctly silent.

═══ 🛑 ③ AND THE EXISTING DETECTION IS INERT ON ALEX'S PLATFORM ═══

`exe_replaced_since_start()` (`service.rs:149`) reads `/proc/self/exe` and tests the link text for a ` (deleted)` suffix. **That is Linux-only.** On macOS the `read_link` fails and it returns `(None, UNKNOWN_NOTE)` — so `served_by.stale` is **never `true` on a Mac**, only `unknown`.

⇒ Alex's situation is strictly worse than this session's. On Linux the skew at least reported `stale: true` six times. On macOS the mechanism built to catch exactly this is silently non-functional, which is why nothing surfaced it to him. **`(dev, inode)` compared at attach is plain POSIX and works on both**, which is a second, independent argument for that comparand over either the version string or the `(deleted)` marker.

═══ ④ THE CLASS: FIVE RESPONSES, ALL DETECTION, ZERO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE ═══

    2026-08-07  a running server cannot say it is stale
    2026-08-0?  reproduced first hand here
    2026-08-08  recurred to the people who wrote it down — cost a day of dogfooding
    2026-08-13  a fresh server on an old build is not stale and stamps confidently
    2026-08-17  AGENTS.md said an mcp reconnect picks up a rebuild; a shared server makes that false
    2026-08-29  this dev session (x6) and Alex

Every response improved REPORTING. **Nothing ever changed what the client DOES.** Same shape as `fact:the-instruction-surface-routes-to-hygiene-and-not-to-whether-the-thing-works`: the information existed and did not reach the person.

═══ 🛑 BOUNDS ═══

NOT ESTABLISHED: what the client should DO on a mismatch. Refuse, warn, or re-elect are three different products, and automatically stopping a daemon another session is mid-write against is not obviously safe — `--stop-shared` accepts that risk deliberately, with a human choosing the moment.

NOT MEASURED: that `cargo build` and `install -m 755` change the inode. It is inferred from the `(deleted)` marker working at all — the marker only appears when a file is unlinked and replaced, so replacement is established for the Linux rebuild path; the macOS installer path is unverified.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether an inode is stable enough in practice — a bind mount, a container layer, or an overlay filesystem could in principle reuse one.

Cargo.toml read 0.42.0 all day and all five daemons published 0.42.0 against 0.42.0 clients, so a version-string check catches ZERO of the six rebuild instances","coverage":{"install_sh_fix":"Alex only","version_string_check":"Alex only","dev_inode_check":"all six, and cross-platform"},"third_finding":"exe_replaced_since_start reads /proc/self/exe and is LINUX-ONLY; on macOS served_by.stale is never true, only unknown - the detection built for this is inert on Alex's platform","class":"five recorded responses, every one improved REPORTING, none changed what the client DOES","not_established":["what the client should do on mismatch - refuse, warn or re-elect are three different products","that cargo build and install -m 755 change the inode: inferred from the (deleted) marker working, not measured; the macOS installer path is unverified","whether an inode is stable enough in practice under bind mounts, container layers or overlay filesystems"]}
